tags.description: Japanese Imperial Navy seaplane tender sunk by US carrier aircraft on 24 September 1944 in Coron Bay. Wreck lies on its port side; upper hull at approx. 22m, deepest sections reported between 36-38m. Advanced wreck diving required.
tags.name: Akitsushima

tags.description: Also known as South Miniloc, El Nido's signature dive site sits in the current-swept channel between Miniloc and Simizu islands, centred on a triangular cabbage-coral garden around 12m with a reported depth range of roughly 5-30m across sources. Moderate to strong current. Best conditions November-May.
tags.name: Biet Point

tags.description: OSM-tagged cave/cavern feature near Matinloc Island, El Nido. No independent dive-shop, forum, or database source could be matched to this specific site at these coordinates during deep QA; the site's identity and the 30m/cave-certification claims are unconfirmed.
tags.name: Cave
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-17: previously marked validated=true on travel-palawan.com, but that source does not describe a distinct named cave dive at these coordinates. No corroborating source found (checked travel-palawan.com, divephilippines.com.ph, puertoparrot.com, asiadivesite.com, philippinedives.com, aquanautelnido.com, elnidohotelsranking.com). Nearest documented feature is Matinloc's 'Secret Beach' underwater crevice (a shallow snorkel-depth swim-through, not a 30m advanced cave dive), which does not match the existing depth/certification claims. Downgraded to unvalidated; site_type/depth left unchanged pending a confirmed source.

tags.description: Southern tip of Matinloc Island in El Nido. Current-swept site known for pelagic activity, with coral-encrusted boulders/rocks descending to 22 meters.
tags.name: Banayan Point
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-17: only one independent source with substantive site-specific content could be confirmed (travel-palawan.com); other apparent sources either mirror the same text or could not be accessed/verified. Below the 3-source bar for this pass -- left validated as-is per policy rather than padding with unverifiable sources. Removed unsourced shark and moray/lionfish/grouper claims from markdown.

tags.description: Also called Picanayas/Pacanayas, on the western side of Matinloc Island in El Nido. Large boulders create corridors where whitetip reef sharks are commonly seen resting; pelagic fish frequently pass through on the current. Depth reported around 6-24 meters.
tags.name: Bikanayos Rock
tags.qa_note: Deep QA 2026-08-17: two independent sources confirmed (travel-palawan.com for sharks/boulders, aquanautelnido.com for depth range as 'Pacanayas'), short of the 3-source bar. Left validated as-is per policy. Removed unsourced grey reef shark, Napoleon wrasse, hawksbill turtle, giant trevally and mackerel claims from markdown. Depth updated from 20m to 24m to match aquanautelnido.com's stated range.

tags.description: Port Barton's signature twin coral formations, a short boat ride from the village. A 2025 reef survey and 2024 press reporting document significant coral loss here from the 2024 mass bleaching event and anchor damage -- reef monitors report the site has lost roughly half its original coral cover. Still snorkeled and dived, but healthy patches are now limited.
tags.name: Twin Reef

tags.description: Port Barton fringing reef, deeper than nearby Twin Reef with more varied coral coloration when healthy. A 2025 reef survey found the reef flat now dominated by macroalgae and dead coral rubble following the 2024 mass bleaching event and water-quality issues in Port Barton Bay, with roughly half or more of surviving coral colonies damaged or dead.
tags.name: Fantastic Reef

tags.description: Smallest and northernmost reef of Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park, roughly 20km north of the main atolls, liveaboard-only and typically dived en route to/from Puerto Princesa (season mid-March to mid-June). Mushroom-shaped structure starts around 7m and drops beyond recreational limits, with unpredictable currents. Known for grey reef and whitetip reef sharks, barracuda, Spanish mackerel, Napoleon wrasse, and schooling unicornfish/surgeonfish.
tags.name: Jesse Beazley Reef
